entries.task_id: this pidgin|is|involved in a reconstructing continuum with its major lexifier
entries.description: this pidgin is involved in a reconstructing continuum with its major lexifier
entries.subject: this pidgin
entries.object: involved in a reconstructing continuum with its major lexifier

spans.text: In addition, another factor that makes it hard to evaluate the boundaries of Juba Arabic as a linguistic entity is that this pidgin is involved in a reconstructing continuum with its major lexifier, which is Northern Sudanese Arabic (or Sudanese Standard Arabic).

spans.text: In addition, another factor that makes it hard to evaluate the boundaries of Juba Arabic as a linguistic entity is that this pidgin is involved in a reconstructing continuum with its major lexifier, which is Northern Sudanese Arabic (or Sudanese Standard Arabic).

entries.description: of Africa began soon after the death of the prophet Muhammad
entries.subject: of Africa
entries.object: soon after the death of the prophet Muhammad

spans.text: The Arab conquest of Africa began soon after the death of the prophet Muhammad.

entries.task_id: the sudan|is|concerned
entries.description: the Sudan is concerned
entries.subject: the Sudan
entries.object: concerned

spans.text: As far as the Sudan is concerned, the penetration of Arab groups from the Upper Nile started in the 12th century and reached its climax by the end of the 15th century.

entries.task_id: and arabic|became|the lingua franca of the area
entries.description: and Arabic became the lingua franca of the area
entries.subject: and Arabic
entries.object: the lingua franca of the area

spans.text: Powerful states, such as the Funj Sultanate and the Muslim Sultanate of Dar Fur, gradually took the place of the ancient Christian Nubian kingdoms, and Arabic became the lingua franca of the area.

entries.task_id: of what|is|now modern sudan
entries.description: of what is now modern Sudan
entries.subject: of what
entries.object: now modern Sudan

spans.text: In 1820 the Khedive of Egypt Muhammad Ali sent a military expedition against the Mamluks who had sheltered in Nubia and eventually conquered a great part of what is now modern Sudan.

entries.task_id: slave traders|started|to set up permanent trading camps
entries.description: slave traders started to set up permanent trading camps
entries.subject: slave traders
entries.object: to set up permanent trading camps

spans.text: The way to southern Sudan was opened for long-distance trade: ivory and slave traders started to set up permanent trading camps, called zaribas (literally ‘cattle enclosure’), which spread all over the White Nile Basin, the Bahr al-Ghazal and Equatorial Province.

entries.task_id: local inhabitants|started|to join the camps deliberately
entries.description: local inhabitants started to join the camps deliberately
entries.subject: local inhabitants
entries.object: to join the camps deliberately

spans.text: Soon afterwards the traders’ camps were progressively turned into military camps and those who had worked in the zaribas as traders’ private troops were gradually incorporated into the government army, while local inhabitants started to join the camps deliberately.

entries.task_id: juba arabic|has|gradually begun to be acquired as a first language
entries.description: Juba Arabic has gradually begun to be acquired as a first language
entries.subject: Juba Arabic
entries.object: gradually begun to be acquired as a first language

spans.text: Thus, even if it is only in the last thirty years that Juba Arabic has gradually begun to be acquired as a first language, it has long been a vehicular medium widely used in inter-ethnic exchanges.

entries.description: Urban speakers are generally more affected by the interference of Sudanese Arabic
entries.subject: Urban speakers
entries.object: generally more affected by the interference of Sudanese Arabic

spans.text: Urban speakers are generally more affected by the interference of Sudanese Arabic; thus, they are to be considered the repositories of the acrolectal/mesolectal varieties.

spans.text: By contrast, the basilectal varieties of Juba Arabic can generally be associated with rural speakers who are more influenced by the Nilotic substratum.

spans.text: Vowel quantity is not distinctive, either lexically or grammatically, although long allophonic variants are found in acrolectal registers; vowel length is also predictable in stressed syllables, and it can be prompted by pragmatic factors such as emphasis.
